title: Elastic Reservation Playbook & Sprint Commitments for Q3 Capacity Experiments
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and sprint-level commitments to test elastic reservation strategies for Dedicated pools. The playbook will define reservation window sizing, hedging lanes, prewarm heuristics, and canary rollout criteria. Outcome: a repeatable process that product, infra, and ops teams can run each quarter to safely reduce committed spend while preserving SLOs for customers on Dedicated SKUs.
acceptance_criteria: Ship a one-page runbook describing 3 elastic reservation policies and decision criteria
Run 2 cross-team simulations that validate latency and error budgets under each policy
Publish cost delta model (expected $/token change) for each policy and include break-even analysis
Create CI job that gates canary rollout metrics and auto-rollbacks for production experiments
notes: Trade-off: tighter hedging reduces reserved spend but increases risk of fallthrough to burst pools; define explicit thresholds for fallback to burst capacity.
Decision pending: default prewarm window (30m vs 2h) — engineering prefers 30m for cost, SRE prefers 2h for tail latency safety.
Will coordinate with Billing on SKU mapping for fractional reservations; finance needs 2-week lead time for pricing experiments.
comments: 2026-01-14 Sofia Patel: Drafted initial scope and shared with Infra/Platform leads. Asked ENG to run historical trace sampling for warmup patterns.
2026-01-20 Miguel Alvarez: Confirmed ENG will provide two synthetic traffic profiles (burst-heavy & steady-medium) by 2026-01-27.
2026-01-28 Priya Desai (SRE): Proposed canary metric set: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, queue length, and shortfall-to-reservation. Added suggestion to include cost-per-token delta.
2026-02-02 Product review: Agreed to prioritize policy A (fractional warm pockets) for the first sprint; policy B (elastic windows with delayed hedging) moved to sprint 2.
2026-02-02 Link: Simulation results uploaded to Drive - drive.redwood.ai/elastic-sims/v2/results-summary.pdf
implementation_plan: Sprint 1 (2 weeks): finalize playbook text, build simulation harness, run baseline against steady-medium profile
Sprint 2 (2 weeks): run burst-heavy simulation, refine hedging thresholds, integrate canary gating into CI
Sprint 3 (2 weeks): small production canary on 10% of traffic with auto-rollback rules; collect telemetry and cost signals
Post-sprint: retrospective, publish playbook as 'elastic-reservations-v1' and schedule quarterly cadence
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: underestimating tail latency impact when reducing prewarm windows. Mitigation: require a stricter canary p99 guardrail and keep instantaneous burst fallback enabled.
Risk: billing SKU mismatch for fractional reservations. Mitigation: involve Billing team early and create a temporary tagging mechanism for experiments.
Risk: operator unfamiliarity with rollback playbook. Mitigation: include runbook run-through session during Sprint 2 and create a one-click rollback dashboard.
Risk: customer confusion about capacity behavior. Mitigation: prepare customer-facing FAQ and proactive mailing list for impacted enterprise customers.
